questions.prompt: A valid certificate for www.example.com has been uploaded to App Service, and the custom hostname is mapped, but HTTPS still does not use it. What configuration is missing?

options.text: A TLS binding associating the hostname with the certificate.
options.explanation: Upload stores the certificate; the binding selects it for the hostname.

options.text: Only another copy of the same certificate file.
options.explanation: Duplicate upload does not create the missing binding.

options.text: Only a larger App Service instance count.
options.explanation: Worker count does not associate a certificate with a hostname.

options.text: Only a DNS TTL of zero.
options.explanation: TTL does not configure the app TLS binding.

questions.prompt: An app requires a wildcard certificate covering *.example.com. Which certificate approach fits App Service requirements?

options.text: Import or upload a suitable wildcard certificate from a certificate provider.
options.explanation: A supported certificate with the required names can be bound to the app.

options.text: Request a free App Service managed wildcard certificate.
options.explanation: The free managed certificate does not support wildcards.

options.text: Use the default azurewebsites.net certificate for example.com.
options.explanation: The default certificate does not cover the custom domain.

options.text: Create only an ownership TXT record and omit TLS binding.
options.explanation: Domain ownership verification does not provide wildcard TLS.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an SNI TLS binding in App Service?

options.text: Select the certificate by hostname while sharing an IP address.
options.explanation: Server Name Indication communicates the requested hostname during TLS.

options.text: Require a separate dedicated IP for every hostname.
options.explanation: That is not the purpose of SNI.

options.text: Automatically create all external DNS records.
options.explanation: TLS binding does not administer the DNS provider.

options.text: Encrypt application data stored on the filesystem.
options.explanation: A TLS binding protects transport connections, not filesystem storage.
